extracted.intended_audience: auditors, institutional financial aid/compliance officers at institutions receiving Federal student financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate institutional compliance with Title IV and related student financial assistance program requirements, including calculation and return of Title IV funds, reporting student status changes, loan servicing, and internal control over Federal programs. Guidance is aimed at planning and performing audits and at helping institutions design controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Withdrawal Date
rubrics_metrics.description: If an institution is required to take attendance the withdrawal date is the last date of academic attendance as determined by the institution from its attendance records. If an institution is not required to take attendance, the withdrawal date is: (1) the date that the student began the withdrawal process prescribed by the school; (2) the date that the student otherwise provided official notification to the school, in writing or orally, of his or her intent to withdraw; (3) if the student ceases attendance without providing official notification to the institution of his or her withdrawal, the midpoint of the payment period or, if applicable, the period of enrollment; (4) if the institution determines that a student did not begin the withdrawal process or otherwise notify the school of the intent to withdraw due to illness, accident, grievous personal loss or other circumstances beyond the student's control, the date the institution determines is related to that circumstance; (5) if a student does not return from an approved leave of absence, the date that the institution determines the student began the leave of absence; or (6) if the student takes an unapproved leave of absence, the date that the student began the leave of absence (34 CFR sections 668.22(c) and (d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions required to take attendance: use attendance records. For non-attendance-taking institutions follow the six-step hierarchy. See 34 CFR §668.22(c),(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of Amount of Title IV Assistance Earned
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount earned is calculated by determining the percentage of Title IV grant or loan assistance earned by the student and applying that percentage to the total Title IV assistance that was or could have been disbursed to the student for the payment period/period of enrollment as of the student's withdrawal date. A student earns 100 percent if withdrawal date is after completion of 60 percent of the payment period/period of enrollment; otherwise percentage earned equals percentage of period completed as of withdrawal date. The unearned amount is the complement of the earned percentage (34 CFR section 668.22(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the earned percentage to total Title IV funds disbursed or could have been disbursed as of withdrawal date. Use the 60% threshold for full earn. Document calculations and reference 34 CFR §668.22(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Payment Period vs Period of Enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of Title IV funds if a student withdraws must be determined on a payment period basis for standard term-based programs (semester/trimester/quarter). For non-term or nonstandard term programs treatment may be determined on either a payment period basis or a period-of-enrollment basis (34 CFR section 668.22(e)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions operating non-term programs may choose the basis but must apply it consistently; if choosing payment-period basis while charging for a longer period, special charge-proration rules apply (see Institutional Return guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of Payment Period or Period of Enrollment Completed (credit-hour and clock-hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: For credit-hour programs: divide total number of calendar days in the period into the number of calendar days completed as of withdrawal date. For clock-hour programs: divide total clock hours in the period into number of clock hours (a) completed by the student as of withdrawal date, or (b) scheduled to be completed as of withdrawal date if clock hours completed are not less than 70 percent of hours scheduled to be completed. Exclude schedule breaks of at least five consecutive days from totals (34 CFR section 668.22(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count all days in period except excluded breaks. For clock-hour programs apply the 70% consideration when scheduled hours exceed completed hours. Maintain supporting schedules demonstrating the numerator/denominator used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution's Return of Unearned Title IV Aid
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution must return the lesser of: (1) the total amount of unearned Title IV assistance to be returned (calculated as total disbursed as of institutional determination less earned amount); or (2) an amount equal to total institutional charges incurred by the student for the payment period or period of enrollment multiplied by the percentage of Title IV assistance not earned. For non-term programs that choose payment-period calculations but charge for a longer period, 'total institutional charges incurred by the student for the payment period' is the greater of the prorated amount of institutional charges for the longer period or the amount of Title IV assistance retained for institutional charges as of the student's withdrawal date (34 CFR section 668.22(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must compute both amounts and return the lesser. Document the institutional charges used, any proration, and retained Title IV amounts. Follow 34 CFR §668.22(g) for non-term/proration specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student's Return of Unearned Title IV Aid (Student Repayments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount the student is responsible for returning equals the total amount of unearned Title IV assistance to be returned minus the amount the institution is required to return. The institution's responsibilities in managing student repayments are detailed in 34 CFR section 668.22(h)(4) (34 CFR section 668.22(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must calculate student repayment obligation, document communications and repayment arrangements, and follow regulatory requirements for collection and handling of student repayments per §668.22(h)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation Order for Return of Title IV Funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns of Title IV funds must be distributed in the prescribed order and that order must be followed regardless of the school's agreements with other State or private agencies (34 CFR section 668.22(i)). Prescribed order: 1) Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loan; 2) Subsidized Federal Stafford Loan; 3) Unsubsidized Federal Direct Stafford Loan; 4) Subsidized Federal Direct Stafford Loan; 5) Federal Perkins Loan; 6) Federal PLUS; 7) Federal Direct PLUS; 8) Federal Pell Grant; 9) Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant; 10) Other SFA Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply returns sequentially to the program list. Trace disbursements and refunds to ensure funds were applied to the correct program in the correct order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Return of Title IV Funds and Determination of Withdrawal Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns of Title IV funds must be deposited to SFA accounts or returned to appropriate FFEL lender within 30 days after the date the institution determines that the student withdrew. An institution must determine the withdrawal date for a student who withdraws without providing notification no later than 30 days after the end of the earlier of: (1) the payment period/period of enrollment, (2) the academic year in which the student withdrew, or (3) the educational program from which the student withdrew (34 CFR section 668.22(o)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must track determination dates and ensure funds/returns occur within 30 days. Maintain documentation showing date of institutional determination and timing of transfers/returns. (Note: text contains a typographical citation; follow applicable CFR.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Objective: Refunds/Returns of Title IV Funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the institution is making refunds/returns of Title IV funds in the proper amount and in a timely manner and is applying the refunds/returns of Title IV funds to Federal programs as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit should assess compliance with calculation, allocation order, timing, and application of returns to programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested Audit Procedures for Title IV Refunds/Returns
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Identify a sample of students who withdrew or dropped out during the audit period and review refund/return determinations/calculations for conformity with requirements. b. Trace refunds/returns to disbursement and accounting records (including canceled checks to lenders and students) to verify application to programs in required order, disbursements when applicable, and that credits/payments were made within required time frames. c. For students with no refunds/returns made, review academic records to ascertain whether the students completed the payment/enrollment period; for students with all failing/incomplete grades, review attendance records to ascertain dropout status and refund entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform sampling of withdrawals, reperform calculations, verify supporting documentation (attendance, charge ledgers, disbursement records), and inspect canceled checks or lender credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Status Changes Reporting (HEAL, FFEL, Direct Loan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each school must notify the holder of the HEAL loan of any change in student's enrollment status within 30 days following the change. Under FFEL and Direct Loan, schools must complete and return within 30 days student status confirmation reports sent by NSLDS. Unless the school expects to complete its next student status report within 60 days, the school must notify NSLDS within 30 days if it discovers a borrower who did not enroll or ceased to be enrolled at least half-time (HEAL: 42 CFR §60.53; FFEL: 34 CFR §682.610; Direct Loan: 34 CFR §685.309).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process has moved to electronic SSCRs; institutions determine frequency of SSCR receipt, must correct and submit changes electronically. Maintain records of notifications and SSCR submissions, showing timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Objective and Suggested Procedures for Student Status Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit Objective: Determine whether the institution is promptly notifying lenders or NSLDS of changes in student status in a timely and accurate manner. Suggested Procedures: a. Select sample of HEAL borrowers who graduated/withdrew/dropped out and verify lender notifications within required timeframe. b. Select sample of FFEL/Direct Loan borrowers who graduated/withdrew/dropped out and verify reporting to lender or inclusion in SSCR within required timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine correspondence, electronic submissions, and timestamps; verify adherence to 30/60 day rules and document any exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Loan Repayments: Repayment Terms and Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: FPL, HPSL/PCL and NSL loans (prior to Nov 13, 1998) are repayable in equal or graduated installments over a 10-year period. HPSL loans made on or after Nov 13, 1998: repayment period not less than 10 and not more than 25 years. NSL loans after Nov 13, 1998 may extend repayment for 10 years under certain conditions. Repayment begins after grace periods (timing varies by loan type) and institutions must establish repayment plans for FPL loans (statutory citations provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify repayment start dates, terms, and that institutions established required repayment plans. Apply applicable statutory/regulatory references for loan type and origination date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan Deferments and Cancellations Eligibility and Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Borrowers may be eligible for deferments or cancellations under specific circumstances (e.g., certain student statuses, qualifying employment, military/volunteer service, death or disability). To qualify, borrower must submit a written request with required documentation to the institution by the institution's established date. Specific requirements vary by loan type and origination date (refer to FPL, HPSL, NSL regulatory sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must have documented procedures and evidence for processing deferment/cancellation requests, including timelines and documentation retained for audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due Care and Diligence in Loan Collection (FPL, HPSL, NSL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must exercise due care and diligence in loan collection. For FPL this includes: (1) conduct an exit interview before borrower leaves and contact borrower a minimum of three times during nine-month grace periods (or two times for six-month grace periods) (34 CFR §674.42); (2) specific billing procedures to notify borrowers of overdue payments and demand overdue amounts (34 CFR §674.43); (3) specific collection procedures including litigation where appropriate (34 CFR §674.45).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review evidence of exit interviews, documented contact attempts, billing notices, and collection actions. Ensure policies and practices match regulatory prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Objective and Suggested Procedures for Loan Repayment/Collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit Objective: Determine whether institutions are processing deferment/cancellation requests and servicing loans as required. Suggested Procedures: a. Select sample of loans entering repayment and verify timely conversion and establishment of repayment plans. b. Review institution's requirements for deferment/cancellation documentation and test a sample for adequate support. c. Select sample of defaulted loans and review loan records to confirm required interviews, contacts, billing and collection procedures were performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace loan lifecycle events, inspect borrower files, and confirm actions match institution's policies and regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Work-Study (FWS) Agreements Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: FWS students may be employed by the institution, Federal/State/local agency, private not-for-profit, or private for-profit organization but employment must not: (1) impair existing service contracts; (2) displace employees; (3) fill jobs vacant due to strikes; or (4) involve construction/operation/maintenance of facilities used for religious worship/sectarian instruction. The institution must enter into a written agreement with any agency/organization providing employment under FWS (34 CFR §§675.20–675.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit by sampling participating students to confirm written employer agreements were executed and jobs meet program restrictions (no displacement, strikes, sectarian facility work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Objective for FWS Agreements and Suggested Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit Objective: Determine whether written agreements with employers are made as required. Suggested Procedure: Select a sample of participating students and ascertain if written agreements with the employers were executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect employer agreements for required terms and signatures; verify employment duties against allowed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borrower Data Transmission and Reconciliation (Direct Loan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must report all loan disbursements and submit required records to the Direct Loan Servicing System (DLSS) via the Loan Origination Center (LOC) within 30 days of disbursement. LOC provides DLSAS data files (Cash Summary, Cash Detail, optional Loan Detail) monthly; schools are required to reconcile these files to the institution's financial records. Instructions and borrower info are available online (34 CFR §§685.102(b), 685.301, 685.303).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may receive up to three DLSAS files monthly for open program years. Reconciliation must be performed monthly and discrepancies investigated and resolved promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Objectives and Suggested Procedures for DLSS Reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit Objectives: Determine whether institutions are reconciling DLSAS data files to institutional records each month and whether DLSS disbursement dates/amounts are supported by institution records. Suggested Procedures: a. Test a sample of DLSAS reconciliations to ascertain reconciliations are performed. b. Test a sample of borrowers to verify DLSS disbursement dates/amounts are supported by institution records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain DLSAS files, reconciliation workpapers, and borrower disbursement documentation; verify adjustments and unresolved items are tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pell Adjustment Timing and Auditor Role
rubrics_metrics.description: All Pell Payment Data for an award year must be submitted by September 30 after the award year. Adjustments for Pell grants not claimed by Sept 30 can be made if the first audit report for the period in which the unclaimed Pell grants were made contains a finding that the institution made proper Pell awards for which it has not received reimbursement or credit. Dear Colleague Letter (P-97-2) provides instructions and describes auditor responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors may be asked to perform additional work to support Pell adjustments; follow Dear Colleague Letter P-97-2 and document findings supporting late Pell adjustment claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirements: Regular Student Enrolled or Accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular student enrolled or accepted for enrollment in an eligible program (34 CFR 600.2, 668.32, 690.75, 675.9, 676.9, 674.9, 682.201, 685.200; 42 CFR 60.5, 57.206(a), 57.306(a), 57.2804).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify enrollment status and program eligibility documentation per cited CFR sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: U.S. Citizen or National
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm citizenship documentation (e.g., SSN, citizenship attestation) is on file where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Has Financial Need
rubrics_metrics.description: Student has financial need as defined by program regulations (34 CFR 675.9, 676.9, 674.9, 682.201, 685.200; 42 CFR 60.51(f), 57.206, 57.306(b), 57.2804(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review FAFSA/need analysis, EFC calculations, and supporting income documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Does Not Owe a Refund on Certain Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Student does not owe a refund on a grant awarded under the Pell Grant or FSEOG programs (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check institutional records and NSLDS for outstanding grant refund obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Not in Default on Any Student Loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Student is not in default on any student loans (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Query NSLDS and lender records to verify default status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Student must maintain good standing or satisfactory progress (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) policy, academic records, and SAP determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Registered for Selective Service (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Student has registered under Section 3 of the Military Selective Service Act where required (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm registration where applicable for male students required to register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Correct Social Security Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Student has a correct social security number (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify SSN matches Social Security Administration records and FAFSA entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: High School Diploma or GED
rubrics_metrics.description: Student possesses a high school diploma or GED (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect transcripts, diplomas, or documented ability-to-benefit evidence where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Above Age of Compulsory School Attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Student is above the age of compulsory school attendance in the State where the institution is located (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm age documentation and state compulsory attendance thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Ability to Benefit (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Student meets 'Ability to Benefit' criteria per 34 CFR Part 668 Subpart J and related regulations (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For students without high school diploma/GED, verify valid Ability-to-Benefit test or program-based criteria are documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: In Need of a Loan/Scholarship to Pursue Study
rubrics_metrics.description: Student is in need of a loan (scholarship) to pursue a course of study at the school (42 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document financial need per program rules when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: SAR/Determination of Eligibility for Pell (undergraduate)
rubrics_metrics.description: An undergraduate student has received for award year a SAR or determination of eligibility/ineligibility for a Pell Grant (34 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify institutional files contain SAR or documentation of Pell eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Not Incarcerated
rubrics_metrics.description: Student is not incarcerated (34 CFR 668.32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm incarceration status where relevant; some programs disallow incarcerated recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Enrollment Limits for Certain Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrolled at least half-time in a course necessary for enrollment in an eligible program for not longer than one 12-month period (34 CFR 668.32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify hours and course sequencing to ensure compliance with period limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Parent PLUS Loan Eligibility Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parents can receive a PLUS loan if conditions are met (34 CFR 682.201, 685.200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review PLUS application and eligibility documentation; check credit and other regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Exceptional Financial Need (where required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptional financial need must be demonstrated for certain programs (42 CFR 57.2804(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document criteria and supporting financial information used to determine exceptional need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Eligibility Requirement: Not Recipient of Conflicting Scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: Cannot be recipient of a National Health Services Corps Scholarship or Indian Health Scholarship as specified (42 CFR 57.2804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify scholarship history and determine program conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Control Objectives for Federal Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives: (1) Transactions properly recorded and accounted for to permit preparation of reliable financial statements/Federal reports, maintain accountability over assets, and demonstrate compliance; (2) Transactions executed in compliance with laws/regulations/contracts/grant agreements that could have direct and material effect on a Federal program and any other laws/regulations in the compliance supplements; (3) Funds, property, and other assets safeguarded against loss from unauthorized use or disposition (as found in §.105 of OMB Circular A-133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors must obtain understanding of internal control sufficient to plan audits and to support assessed level of control risk; entities should design controls to achieve these objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components and Characteristics: Control Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Control Environment sets tone and foundation of internal control. Characteristics include: sense of ethical operations (code of conduct), Board/Audit Committee oversight, management responsiveness to prior questioned costs and recommendations, management respect for compliance requirements, clearly defined key managers' responsibilities, adequate knowledge/experience of key managers, staff knowledgeable about compliance and responsible to report noncompliance, management commitment to competence/training, management support of adequate information/reporting systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether these characteristics exist and are operating; consider written policies (codes), documented responsibilities, training records, and evidence of board/audit committee activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components and Characteristics: Risk Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk Assessment involves identification and analysis of risks to achievement of objectives. Characteristics include: program managers/staff understanding key compliance objectives, organizational structure identifying risks of noncompliance, assignment of responsibility to identify/communicate changes, identification of employees needing supervision, management identification/assessment of complex operations/projects, awareness of monitoring/audit results and related risks, and processes to implement changes in program objectives/procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm existence of risk identification processes, documentation of assessed risks, and mechanisms to respond to monitoring/audit findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components and Characteristics: Control Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Control Activities are policies/procedures ensuring management directives are carried out. Characteristics include: clearly written/communicated operating policies; procedures to implement changes in laws/regulations/guidance/funding agreements; prohibition against overriding controls; adequate segregation of duties between performance/review/recordkeeping; computer controls (data entry edit checks, exception reporting, access controls, input/output reviews, general/security controls); supervision commensurate with competence; personnel with adequate knowledge/experience; securing and inventorying assets; board meetings reviewing financial information with written documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess presence of written procedures, segregation of duties matrices, IT control documentation, asset safeguarding procedures, and supervisory structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components and Characteristics: Information and Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification, capture, and exchange of information in timely form. Characteristics: accounting system that separately identifies Federal and non-Federal transactions and allocates shared transactions; adequate source documentation to support reported amounts; recordkeeping to retain documentation for required periods; timely reports to managers for review/action; accurate information accessible to those who need it; reconciliations and reviews ensure report accuracy; established internal/external communication channels (staff meetings, bulletin boards, memos, email, surveys); communicated duties and control responsibilities; channels to report suspected improprieties and actions taken; established channels between pass-through entities and subrecipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect systems for fund coding, retention schedules, communication logs, and evidence of reconciliations and supervisory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components and Characteristics: Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring assesses quality of internal control over time. Characteristics include ongoing monitoring via independent reconciliations, staff feedback, rotating staff, supervisory reviews; periodic site visits for decentralized/subrecipient locations; follow-up on irregularities/deficiencies; internal quality control reviews; management meetings with program monitors/auditors; internal audit testing for compliance; Board review of monitoring/audit results and corrective actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify monitoring schedules, internal audit reports, follow-up actions, and evidence that monitoring results are communicated to management/board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control Objectives and Characteristics: Activities Allowed or Unallowed / Allowable Costs and Cost Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Control Objective: provide reasonable assurance that Federal awards are expended only for allowable activities and that costs charged to Federal awards are allowable per applicable cost principles. Control Environment: management sets reasonable budgets and enforces penalties for misuse, organization-wide awareness of need for separate identification of Federal costs, management provides approvers with lists of allowable/unallowable expenditures. Risk Assessment: process for assessing risks from cost accounting changes and key managers understanding potential mischarging areas. Control Activities: accountability for charges between Federal/non-Federal, process for timely updating procedures for changes in allowable activities/cost principles, accuracy checks on computations, supporting documentation comparison to allowable lists, adjustments for unallowable costs, segregation of duties, accountability assigned to knowledgeable individual. Information & Communication: budget-to-actual reports provided timely, communication channels on activities/costs allowed, training programs on allowable costs, access to grant agreements and cost principles. Monitoring: management reviews supporting documentation, comparisons with budget/expectations, analytic reviews and audits performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should maintain lists of allowable/unallowable costs, control procedures for pre-audit/approval, and documentation of reviews. Auditors should test transactions for allowability and verify controls to prevent mischarging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control Objectives and Characteristics: Cash Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Control Objective: provide reasonable assurance that Federal cash drawdowns are only for immediate needs, States comply with Treasury agreements, and recipients limit payments to subrecipients to immediate cash needs. Control Environment: appropriate assignment of approval responsibility for drawdowns/payments, budgets consistent with cash needs. Risk Assessment: mechanisms to anticipate events affecting cash needs, routine assessment of subrecipient cash needs, identification of programs receiving cash advances and awareness of cash management requirements. Control Activities: cash flow statements by program, accounting system capable of scheduling payments and requests from Treasury to avoid timing gaps, supervisory review, written policies for requesting cash advances close to actual outlays, monitoring cash management, repayment of excess interest, and for State programs written policies detailing agreement coverage, funding methods, interest calculation, and check clearing patterns. Information & Communication: variance reporting of expected vs actual disbursements/drawdowns, communication channels between pass-through entity and subrecipients. Monitoring: periodic independent evaluation of cash management, evaluation of subrecipient fund requests, review of compliance with Treasury-State agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain cash flow analyses, written cash-management policies, and documentation of drawdown timing and reconciliations. Auditors should verify adherence to drawdown timing and reconciliation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control Objectives and Characteristics: Davis-Bacon Act Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Control Objective: provide reasonable assurance that contractors and subcontractors are paid prevailing wage rates for projects covered by the Davis-Bacon Act. Control Environment: management understands and communicates Davis-Bacon requirements and monitoring responsibilities. Risk Assessment: mechanisms to identify contractors/subcontractors most at risk of nonpayment of prevailing wages and identification of monitoring approach. Control Activities: inform contractors in procurement documents of prevailing wage requirements; require contractors/subcontractors to submit certifications and payrolls meeting prevailing wage requirements; monitor payrolls for compliance. Information & Communication: communicate requirements to contractors and subcontractors and obtain required documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect procurement documents, contractor payroll certifications, and monitoring records to ensure prevailing wage compliance.
